textEs: La enzima EcoRI siempre produce extremos romos.
explanation: EcoRI cuts G^AATTC: the top strand after the G and the bottom strand at the mirror position, leaving 4-nt 5′ overhangs (AATT), i.e. sticky ends. Blunt ends come from enzymes that cut both strands at the same point, such as EcoRV (GAT^ATC), SmaI (CCC^GGG) or PvuII (CAG^CTG).

textEs: Los extremos generados por BamHI (G^GATCC) y por BglII (A^GATCT) pueden ligarse entre sí.
textEn: Ends generated by BamHI (G^GATCC) and by BglII (A^GATCT) can be ligated to each other.
explanation: Both enzymes cut after the first base of their site and leave the same 5′-GATC overhang. The recognition sequences differ, but the sticky ends are complementary, so DNA ligase can join them.

textEs: El sitio híbrido que se forma al ligar un extremo BamHI con un extremo BglII puede volver a ser cortado por cualquiera de las dos enzimas.
textEn: The hybrid site formed by ligating a BamHI end to a BglII end can be recut by either of the two enzymes.
explanation: The junction reads GGATCT (or AGATCC in the other orientation). BamHI needs GGATCC and BglII needs AGATCT, so neither recognises the hybrid site. Only enzymes that recognise the 4-bp core GATC, such as Sau3AI or MboI, can still cut it.

textEs: Una enzima con una secuencia de reconocimiento de 6 pb corta, en promedio, una vez cada 4096 pb en una secuencia aleatoria.
textEn: An enzyme with a 6-bp recognition sequence cuts, on average, once every 4096 bp in random sequence.
explanation: Each position matches with probability 1/4, so a given 6-bp sequence appears with probability (1/4)⁶: once every 4⁶ = 4096 bp. For 4-bp sites it is 256 bp, for 8-bp sites (NotI) 65 536 bp.

textEs: Tratar el vector con fosfatasa alcalina impide que se vuelva a circularizar sobre sí mismo durante la ligación.
textEn: Treating the vector with alkaline phosphatase prevents it from recircularising on itself during ligation.
explanation: Alkaline phosphatase removes the 5′ phosphates. DNA ligase joins a 3′-OH to a 5′-phosphate, so the vector's own ends cannot be joined. The insert still carries 5′ phosphates, so it can be ligated in; the two remaining nicks are repaired in E. coli.

textEs: Solo los plásmidos pueden utilizarse como vectores de clonación en E. coli.
textEn: Only plasmids can be used as cloning vectors in E. coli.
explanation: Besides plasmids, E. coli vectors include bacteriophage λ (insertion and replacement vectors), M13, cosmids, and high-capacity vectors such as BACs and P1/PAC vectors.

textEs: Una genoteca con un número de clones igual al tamaño del genoma dividido por el tamaño medio del inserto contiene todos los genes del organismo.
textEn: A library whose number of clones equals the genome size divided by the average insert size contains all the genes of the organism.
explanation: That is one genome-equivalent, but clones are random: some regions are cloned several times and others not at all. By Clarke–Carbon, P = 1 − (1 − f)ᴺ ≈ 1 − 1/e ≈ 63%. For 99% you need about 4.6 genome-equivalents, N = ln(1 − P) / ln(1 − f).

textEs: En un gel de agarosa, la forma superenrollada de un plásmido siempre migra más despacio que su forma lineal.
textEn: In an agarose gel, the supercoiled form of a plasmid always migrates more slowly than its linear form.
explanation: Supercoiled DNA is compact and normally runs faster than the linear form of the same plasmid; the open-circular (nicked) form is the slowest. The exact positions shift with agarose % and the presence of ethidium bromide, which is exactly why a statement with 'siempre' should make you suspicious.

textEs: Según la regla de Wallace, la Tm de un cebador depende únicamente de su longitud.
textEn: According to the Wallace rule, the Tm of a primer depends only on its length.
explanation: Tm = 4(G+C) + 2(A+T): it depends on base composition as well as length, because G–C pairs have three hydrogen bonds and A–T pairs two. Two 20-mers can differ by up to 40 °C (all A/T: 40 °C; all G/C: 80 °C).

textEs: La Taq polimerasa tiene actividad correctora de pruebas (exonucleasa 3′→5′), por lo que no introduce errores durante la PCR.
textEn: Taq polymerase has proofreading (3′→5′ exonuclease) activity, so it introduces no errors during PCR.
explanation: Taq polymerase lacks 3′→5′ exonuclease (proofreading) activity, so misincorporated bases are not removed and PCR products contain occasional errors. When accuracy matters, a proofreading polymerase such as Pfu is used.
